deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 77v is a rough draft of an administrative letter, written in a hasty Kurrent hand with several deletions. It sits on the back of a sheet in the 'Luftwellen' bundle. The next page (78) holds the draft of the general-consequences section of Riemann's 1859 memoir on plane air waves of finite amplitude.

Approximate content of the letter:
- Addressee: the 'hochlöbliche Civilstands-Amt der freien Hansestadt Bremen', i.e. the civil registry office of Bremen.
- Request: the writer 'gehorsamst' asks for issue of a certificate. The word is read 'Todtenschein' (death certificate), though this reading is uncertain.
- Person concerned: the deleted first wording was 'für Fräulein Christine[?] Riemann'. This was replaced by a longer description.
- Details given: a date '29. Dec. 1855'; a reference to the house of 'Postsecretair Riemann' (a further word in parentheses is uncertain); a death at Bremen 'am 28. d. M.'; and the name 'Christiane[?] Emilie Riemann'.
- Fees: the writer asks that fees be collected by postal cash-on-delivery ('durch Postvorschuss').
- Close: the standard formula 'Mit vollkommener Hochachtung / Ew. Wohlgeboren'.

Context: Riemann's brother Wilhelm was a postal official in Bremen. Wilhelm, and also a sister, died in the later 1850s, after which Riemann took responsibility for his surviving sisters. The draft is plausibly connected with those family deaths. The exact person, the role of the 1855 date, and the dates themselves cannot be fixed securely from this hurried draft.

The page is biographical and archival, not mathematical. Its only relevance to the Luftwellen work is that it helps date the paper the drafts were written on (late 1850s, consistent with the 1859 memoir).

results.what: Draft letter to the Bremen civil registry requesting a (death?) certificate for a member of the Riemann family; no mathematical content

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics. It is a personal administrative letter draft, of minor biographical interest only. It is consistent with the known deaths in Riemann's family in Bremen in the later 1850s.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'Todtenscheins[?]' is a plausible reading of the requested document, but remains uncertain.

The phrase before 'Postsecretair' is very uncertain. It may read 'im Hause des ... ' with a word other than 'verstorbenen', so the claim that the postal secretary was already deceased should not be taken from the transcription.
The parenthetical after 'Riemann' is illegible. The reading '(Wilhelm[?] ...)' is a guess, though compatible with Riemann's brother Wilhelm being a Bremen postal official.
Final request line: 'Die Gebühren' with 'Die' struck, then 'bitte ich durch Postvorschuss gefälligst [erheben, struck] zu wollen'. The struck verb is uncertain ('erheben'/'entnehmen').
Name line: the deleted 'Christine Riemann' and the later 'Christiane[?] Emilie Riemann' are both uncertain readings.
